 Sports 
 November 19, 2026 12:14 am 
 Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat speaks to the media during an introductory press conference at Kaseya Center on July 16, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP)
 By  Peter Akinbo 
 Kindly share this story:
 Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo said facing his former team, Milwaukee Bucks, was “just another game” ahead of their meeting at the Kaseya Centre.
 It was the first time in his NBA career that the Greek star played against the Bucks. He spent 13 seasons in Milwaukee, winning two MVP awards and leading the franchise to the 2021 NBA title, when he was also named Finals MVP. His trade to Miami over the summer ended that spell.
 Speaking before the game, Antetokounmpo said he planned to stick to his usual routine.
 “Just another game. I’m gonna do the same thing, eat the same meal. I’m going to kiss my kids. It’s the same thing. Doesn’t matter the jersey,” he said. 
 He added that he had not felt emotional about the reunion. “I haven’t found myself being emotional. I think the only time I’ve been emotional was when we won the championship.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources 
 He also thanked the club and its supporters, saying, “I think I was able to give my heart and soul every single night for the organisation and the fans.” Related News VIDEO: How Kobe, LeBron, Giannis sought my guidance — Hakeem Olajuwon

  The fans were wonderful. 
 “They welcomed me when I was 18 years old; they welcomed my family. My brothers went to school there, my kids were born there, I was pretty much raised there,” he said.
 The Heat went into the game with momentum, having won five straight and eight of their last 10. They beat the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday, with Antetokounmpo contributing 20 points, 13 rebounds and six assists. Miami were 8-6 for the season.
 The Bucks (1-13) came in on a run of 10 straight defeats and had lost 13 of their last 14 games, the most recent a 113-106 loss to the Atlanta Hawks. They arrived with four former Heat players who went the other way in the trade: Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware and Kasparas Jakucionis. Herro was averaging 20.3 points per game, while Klay Thompson had been scoring 17.1 points over Miami’s last 10 games.
 The night also marked the release of the video game GTA VI, with the Heat wearing special uniforms and unveiling a new court for a Vice City theme. It was the first of four meetings between the teams this season, and the next is in Milwaukee on January 28.
 Peter Akinbo
